voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: Phaistos, Crete. July, nineteen-oh-eight. Archaeologists at a Minoan palace found a disc of fired clay, about sixteen centimetres across.
The two faces carry spirals of two hundred and forty-two signs in all. Each one was pressed into the wet clay with a stamp, before firing.
Forty-five different signs. No other disc like it has ever been found.
No trace of the stamps that made it has ever been reported.
It has been read as a prayer, a hymn, a list. More than a century on, no reading has been accepted.
